done_when: A builder round runs those cheap repo checks before it ends, so a failing one is fixed in that same round instead of in CI.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - the regression test runs its second worker round.
The second iteration resumes Claude's saved session, but this assertion requires the full cheap-check instruction in the latest prompt. `src/forge/worker.py:604–640` builds a shortened continuation prompt without reading `templates/brief.md`, and `_claude` sends that prompt when resuming at line 721. Consequently, both fixture cases fail on their second iteration and block CI. Check that the instructions remain available through the initial prompt and resumed conversation instead of requiring the full instruction to be resent.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_workers_run_cheap_checks_before_the_round_ends

why: A builder round that fails a cheap check, such as a file over 1,200 lines, a rule label that collides with another rule's test, or a test with no rule, is found only after the push, which costs a CI wait and a paid fix round.
